questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Franklin's time working in Pennsylvania's printing offices
The history of Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress and its translations
Franklin's career as a sailor and his first voyage to London
Franklin's journey to Philadelphia and his hardships on the way
questions.explain: Franklin narrates the difficult trip by boat and on foot from New York toward Philadelphia.

questions.q: What book did the drunken Dutchman ask Franklin to dry?
questions.explain: It was Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, in Dutch.

questions.q: How long was Franklin on the water crossing to Amboy?
questions.explain: He had been thirty hours on the water without food or drink but filthy rum.

questions.q: How did Franklin treat his fever?
options: Rested in bed for several days
questions.explain: Having read that cold water was good for a fever, he drank it plentifully and sweated it out.

questions.q: Why did people suspect Franklin on his walk to Burlington?
options: He looked so miserable they took him for a runaway servant
He was seen buying gingerbread without enough money to pay
He carried a chest that was thought to be stolen goods
He was a stranger who kept asking about boats to Burlington
questions.explain: He looked so miserable that he was suspected of being a runaway servant.
